questions.question_text: Applying the principles of EBM, which of the following must be considered when choosing a new drug for treating a patient?

options.text: Number of patients to be treated in order to achieve a single case of success
The validity of the evidence for the treatment
All of the other 4 listed options
the generalisability of trial results to your clinical sample
The expected rate of spontaneous resolution in your clinical sample

correct_answer.text: All of the other 4 listed options

questions.explanation:
Applying principles of EBM, one must check for the internal validity of a study and the degree of generalisability before adapting results to
clinical practice. One must also be aware of the fact that though clinically more meaningful, NNTs quoted in RCTs may not translate to the
same extent in actual clinical practice. One way of appreciating the usefulness of a newly introduced drug is to calculate the NNT for one 's
own clinical population (target population). To enable this one may estimate patient expected event rate (PEER) which is given by expected
spontaneous resolution rate or the response rate for an existing standard treatment.

correct_answer.text: Variance of observation is lesser in cross over design

questions.explanation:
As same subjects are used for both active intervention and control intervention, this reduces variance in observations to a signi�cant
degree, increasing the power of the cross over trials.

questions.question_text:
E�ectiveness of an intervention is measured by using pragmatic trials. Considering the trial design, pragmatic trials are usually which one of
the following?
questions.explanation: A pragmatic trial preserves many aspects of an RCT such as randomisation, concealing allocation, etc.

questions.question_text: According to DSM-4, ca�einism is de�ned as recent consumption of ca�eine usually in excess of
questions.explanation:
According to DSM-4, ca�einism is de�ned as recent consumption of ca�eine usually in excess of 250 mg accompanied by �ve or more of the
following; restlessness, nervousness, excitement, insomnia, �ushed face, diuresis, GI disturbance, muscle twitching, rambling �ow of
thought and speech, tachycardia, periods of inexhaustibility, psychomotor agitation, when these symptoms can cause signi�cant distress or
impairment in social, occupational or other important areas of functioning and are not due to a general medical condition or better
accounted for by another medical disorder (e.g. anxiety disorder).

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a feature of Wernicke's encephalopathy?
questions.explanation:
The classical triad of ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and confusion is rarely present in Wernicke's encephalopathy. The syndrome is much more
common than is widely believed. A presumptive diagnosis of Wernicke's encephalopathy should, therefore, be made in any patient
undergoing detoxi�cation who experiences any of the following signs; Ataxia, Hypothermia and hypotension, Confusion, ophthalmoplegia/
Nystagmus, Memory disturbance and coma/unconsciousness.

questions.question_text:
A 64-year-old lady is having problems with alcohol use for many years now. She presents with back pain, nocturia and tiredness. Which of
the following electrolyte disturbance is likely?
questions.explanation: Chronic alcoholism is a predisposing factor for hypocalcemia and is associated with chronic pancreatitis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following potentially dangerous side e�ect is associated with clonidine, when used for treating opioid dependence?
questions.explanation:
Clonidine is not so popular now due to high rates of hypotension associated with it. If the short duration of Opioid withdrawal treatment is
desirable, a2 adrenergic agonists (e.g. clonidine and Lofexidine) are preferable to methadone. As Lofexidine do not control symptoms such
as nausea, additional symptom support using metoclopramide, antidiarrhoeals etc. may be required.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cognitions describe abstinence violation e�ect in those with alcohol dependence?

options.text: I will drink just once; this won't harm me
I had a drink; so I have turned into a drinker again
It is not up to me to change myself

correct_answer.text: I had a drink; so I have turned into a drinker again

questions.explanation:
Abstinence violation e�ect refers to the cognition that "I had a drink; so I am a drinker again'. This may force patients to reinstate full pattern
of drinking.

questions.question_text: Tolerance is least likely to develop for which of the following symptoms of amphetamine use?
questions.explanation:
Regular use of amphetamines induces tolerance to some e�ects, which means that more and more of the drug is required to produce the
desired e�ects. Tolerance does not develop to all e�ects at the same rate, for example to the vasopressor actions.

questions.question_text:
A chronic alcohol abuser presented to A&E with history suggestive of memory impairment and gait disturbance. On examination he has a
malnourished appearance with scaly skin lesions. Which of the following is recommended before discharge?
questions.explanation:
Treatment with intravenous thiamine (B1) is recommended for patients at high risk of Wernicke- Korsako� syndrome. (Pabrinex(r) IVHP 5mL
ampoules three times daily for two days). Following the initial IV loading dose, oral supplementation should include thiamine 100mg three
times daily. If the patient is at risk of malnutrition then oral thiamine 100mg three times daily should continue inde�nitely. There is little
evidence to substantiate the use of Vitamin B Compound Strong tablets.

questions.question_text: The lifetime prevalence of OCD in the general population is
questions.explanation:
A national, community-based survey of OCD in the UK (1993, 10,000 people) found that 1.0% of men and 1.5% of women reported
symptoms in the previous month. A survey of a random sample of people living in private households in the UK (2000, 8580 adults aged 16-
74 years) found that 1.1% of those surveyed reported symptoms of OCD during the previous week. ECA, the epidemiological catchment area
survey carried out in the USA in 1984 (about 10,000 people) found an age- and sex-standardised annual prevalence of OCD in people aged
26 to 64 years of 1.3%, and a lifetime prevalence of 2.3%. Thus, between 2-3% of general population has 'lifetime' history of OCD. The rates
may be higher in children considered alone.

questions.question_text: What percentage of patients on clozapine develop agranulocytosis?
questions.explanation:
It is 0.7%. The risk of Agranulocytosis decreases to 0.07% after the �rst year of treatment. Risk factor includes increasing age and Asian race.
In contrast, the risk of the more benign neutropenia is higher, estimated to be 1-2%.

questions.question_text: The mean age of onset of chronic fatigue syndrome is between
questions.explanation:
The prevalence of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome is nearly 0.5% with a higher rate in women [M-F - 1:3], those belonging to lower occupational
status and educational background. The mean age of onset is between 29-35 years. Mean illness duration is 3-9 years. The prevalence
seems to be lower among children and adolescents.

questions.question_text:
A middle-aged woman who was taking lithium presents with weight gain and constipation along with lethargy. What proportion of those
who take lithium develop hypothyroidism?
questions.explanation:
The prevalence of clinical hypothyroidism during lithium treatment varies between 5 to 10%. The main risk factor is female gender (women
14% v. men 4.5%). Women were at highest risk during the �rst two years of lithium treatment, and women starting lithium aged 40-59 years
had the greatest prevalence (> 20%). [The British Journal of Psychiatry (1999) 175: 336-339]

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement regarding rating scales for depression is true?

options.text: Zung depression scale is observer rated
Geriatric depression scale has more somatic than cognitive items of depression
The maximum score for Hamilton depression scale (17 items) is 52
Beck's depression scale is more sensitive to change than other scales

correct_answer.text: The maximum score for Hamilton depression scale (17 items) is 52

questions.explanation: Zung rating scale is self-rated. Beck's has 21 items. MADRS is the most sensitive to change among commonly used depression scales.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of psychotic illness in patients with epilepsy is;
questions.explanation:
The prevalence of psychotic illness in patients with epilepsy is at least 4%. A diagnosis of temporal lobe epilepsy does not seem to confer
additional risk.

questions.question_text: Which of the following signs is not present in Wernicke's encephalopathy?
questions.explanation:
Wernicke's encephalopathy is an acute condition characterized by well-known triad of ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and global confusional state.
Classic triad of confusion, ataxia and nystagmus is only present in 10% of patients and 80% of patients are not diagnosed before post
mortem. These eye signs are usually bilateral but not necessarily symmetrical. WE is directly caused by acute thiamine de�ciency, due to
inadequate dietary intake, reduced gastrointestinal absorption, decreased hepatic storage, and impaired utilization. Peripheral neuropathy,
a sign of beri-beri, results from more chronic vitamin de�ciency states.

questions.question_text: Compared to the general population, patients with schizophrenia are less likely to die from
questions.explanation:
The relationship between cancer and schizophrenia is not straightforward and can appear paradoxical. For example, tobacco smoking rates
in those with schizophrenia are typically twice those of the background population which would suggest higher rates of lung cancer in those
with schizophrenia, but some studies quote a lower incidence of lung cancer in people with schizophrenia (Hippisley-Cox et al 2007). The
excess mortality in schizophrenia is attributable to cardiovascular, neoplastic and respiratory disease (Leucht et al 2007). People with
schizophrenia are more likely to die prematurely than the general population from both suicide and physical ill health. (Ref: Cancer and
schizophrenia: is there a paradox?- Richard Hodgson, Wildgust & Bushe)

questions.question_text: A man with schizophrenia is on clozapine but is still experiencing active psychotic symptoms. The best drug for augmentation is
questions.explanation:
Clozapine is a polyvalent drug with a comparatively weak dopamine receptor blockade. Therefore, the combined use of substituted
benzamides such as sulpride or Amisulpride that have highly selective dopamine receptor blockade is, in particular, a preferred strategy
(Kerwin, 2005)

questions.question_text: The standardized mortality rate for major depression is
questions.explanation:
The SMR for major depression is 20 times that expected; The mortality rate for manic depression is 15 times higher than the expected
(Harris and Barraclough 1997)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the longevity of patients with schizophrenia is based on epidemiological evidence?

options.text: Most common cause of death is suicide
The mortality rate is climbing down in the last two decades
All patients who die prematurely have a diagnosis of metabolic syndrome
Have higher mortality risk than those with bipolar disorder
Have 2.6 times higher mortality than general population

correct_answer.text: Have 2.6 times higher mortality than general population

questions.explanation:
The SMR is 2.6 for both schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and it is showing a worryingly increasing trend. Gelder et al. (2005) Shorter
Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry, 5th edition pg 294

questions.question_text:
Mr Y was admitted to a neuro-rehabilitation unit for the treatment of brain injury. He was reported to present with spontaneous,
unprovoked crying although he is not depressed. You are requested to review and advise treatment. The drug of choice is;
questions.explanation:
This patient is su�ering from Pathological laughing and crying syndrome, also called emotional incontinence/emotionalism/pseudobulbar
a�ect. This refers to spontaneous, unprovoked laughter or crying seen in patients with brain damage; it occurs in response to non-speci�c
stimuli, in the absence of associated mood change (mood incongruent a�ect) and the absence of voluntary control of facial expression. The
a�ect change is generally transient but distressing due to perceived loss of control. In a study, 66% of people with MS and pathological
laughing/crying responded to 75 mg of amitriptyline per day. Improvement in symptoms also occurs with either amantadine or levodopa
administration. Fluoxetine and sertraline have been evaluated in small parallel RCTs with favourable results; citalopram in a cross over trial
showed signi�cant bene�ts and fewer side-e�ects.

questions.question_text: Which is the most reliable risk factor for completed suicide?
questions.explanation: The strongest risk factor of suicide is DSH history with previous suicide attempts

questions.question_text: The risk of completed suicide in patients with history of deliberate self-harm is
questions.explanation:
The strongest risk factor of suicide is history of deliberate self harm. Prognosis of non-fatal DSH: 20% repeat and 1% die in next year. 10%
eventually complete suicide. The risk of suicide within one year of DSH is 0.7% (nearly 1 in 100); more in males 1.1%; 0.5% in females. This is
66 x the general population risk.(Ref: Emergencies in psychiatry-119)

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychometric tests exploit the personality dynamics that are outside the conscious awareness of the tested subject?
questions.explanation: Thematic Apperception Test is a projective test.

This man is presenting with features of steroid-induced psychosis, due to abuse of anabolic steroids. Athletes and body builders often tend
to use anabolic steroids. They produce euphoriant e�ects, increased muscle mass, muscle strength and a sense of increased energy levels. It
is associated with mental health problems such as psychosis, emotional instability, increased aggressiveness, persecutory/grandiose ideas,
depressive illness and chronic fatigue. Psychotic symptoms are often associated, up to half the cases. (Ref: Oxford handbook of psychiatry-
547)

questions.question_text: Most cases of postpartum psychosis develop in which of the following postpartum periods?
questions.explanation:
Postpartum psychosis occurs in 1 –2/1000 childbearing women within the �rst two weeks after delivery. In some patients, as early as 2 –3
days after childbirth, paranoid, grandiose, or bizarre delusions, mood swings, confused thinking, and grossly disorganized behavior that
represent a dramatic change from previous functioning may be seen. It is far less common than postpartum depression which a�ects 10% –
13% of new mothers, and the maternity blues, which a�ects 50% –75% of postpartum women.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rating scales employ Life Change Units?
questions.explanation:
To measure stress according to the Holmes and Rahe Social Readjustment Scale, the number of "Life Change Units" that apply to events in
the past year of an individual's life is employed.

questions.question_text: Number of people su�ering from mixed anxiety and depressive symptoms at any given time in UK is
questions.explanation:
According to some studies, mixed anxiety and depression is one of the most common mental disorder in Britain with nearly 9% of people
meeting criteria for diagnosis - The O�ce for National Statistics Psychiatric Morbidity report (2001). "Mixed anxiety and depressive
symptoms that do not reach thresholds for formal psychiatric diagnosis make up nearly half of all psychological problems in the UK and are
nearly four times more common than depressive disorder alone". Walters, K., Buszewicz, M., Weich, S., & King, M. (2011). Mixed anxiety and
depressive disorder outcomes: prospective cohort study in primary care. The British Journal of Psychiatry, 198(6), 472-478.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychiatric disorder is projected to become the second largest cause of disease burden worldwide by 2020?
questions.explanation:
Unipolar depression will rank second while bipolar disorder in sixth place when global disease burden are considered in 2020, according to
current projections.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of epilepsy in patients with schizophreniform psychosis is:
questions.explanation: The point prevalence is between 0.4-1%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the trend shown by the epidemiology of depression?

options.text: Point prevalence is steady across years
Detection of depression is not in�uenced by local vernacular spoken
Middle aged men are increasingly having more depression
Highest risk for depression is in those over age 30 yrs

questions.explanation:
Various studies including NCS and its replication NCS-R, NSEARC and ECA have implicated that lifetime prevalence of depression is
increasing.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of depression in patients with Coronary Heart Disease is
questions.explanation:
The prevalence rate of clinically signi�cant depression among patients with coronary heart disease is approximately 21.5%. The risk of
clinical depression in patients with CHD is 2-3 times the rate of the general population.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Y-BOCS (Yale-Brown obsessive compulsive scale) is not true?

options.text: Rating is on a 4 point scale

questions.explanation:
Y-BOCS does not rate obsessive personality traits. The Y-BOCS is a clinician administered semi-structured interview that rates obsessions
and compulsions separately on time occupied, distress, impairment, resistance, and control. It is now considered as the scale of choice for
rating OCD symptoms.

questions.question_text: The Yale-Brown obsessive-compulsive scale covers all of the following aspects except
questions.explanation:
YBOCS, the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale, is the preferred measurement tool for measuring the severity and nature of OCD
symptoms. It does not measure anankastic traits.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs is contraindicated in renal failure?
questions.explanation: Amisulpride is renally excreted almost exclusively. Hence renal failure will be a contraindication to use this drug.

questions.question_text:
According to CATIE study of patients with Schizophrenia, the number of patients meeting criteria for metabolic syndrome, ranges between
what percentages;
questions.explanation:
The prevalence of metabolic syndrome was 40.9% to 42.7% according to two di�erent criteria used for the diagnosis of metabolic syndrome
in the CATIE sample. Interestingly, the prevalence was higher in women 54.2% than in men (36.0%).

questions.question_text: Which of the following may help di�erentiating borderline personality from bipolar disorder?

options.text: Impulsivity in bipolar disorder is chronic rather than episodic
Mood changes lasts for many days in borderline personality
Emptiness is often used as the mood descriptor in borderline personality
Borderline personality has a de�nite onset
Elated mood shifts are often seen in borderline personality

correct_answer.text: Emptiness is often used as the mood descriptor in borderline personality

questions.explanation:
In Bipolar Disorder the onset is in early 20s (later than borderline), mood changes are observable spontaneoulsy rather than being
precipitated solely by external events, if present, episodic self harm attempts are usually related to depression, though self mutilation is
rare. Patients with borderline PD use 'emptiness' as a descriptor for their mood more often than those with bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct with respect to automatism?

options.text: Sane automatism is due to internal causes
Epileptic automatism is classi�ed as insane automatism
Automatism is commonly seen in REM sleep behavioural disorder
Subjects cannot have complete acquittal when making a plea of automatism

correct_answer.text: Epileptic automatism is classi�ed as insane automatism

questions.explanation:
Automatism is not a common plea. Insane automatism is due to internal causes such as epilepsy - these are seen as irreversible and may
lead to psychiatric disposal if required. Sane automatisms can lead to complete acquittal if internal factors are ruled out - i.e. recurrence risk
is low. In REM sleep behavioural disordered, organised actions leading to automatisms are extremely rare.

questions.question_text:
Miss. Y is a 24-year-old woman recently diagnosed with debilitating symptoms of premenstrual syndrome. She asks for a prescription of
�uoxetine. Which of the following is an accurate statement in this context?

options.text: Fluoxetine provides relief only after continuous use for at least 5 cycles of menstruation
Fluoxetinehas no evidence in treating premenstrual syndrome
Fluoxetine provides relief in premenstrual syndrome irrespective of its e�ect on depressive features
Fluoxetine provides relief in premenstrual syndrome through its antidepressant activity
Fluoxetine is the only antidepressant that has been studied for use in premenstrual dyndrome

correct_answer.text: Fluoxetine provides relief in premenstrual syndrome irrespective of its e�ect on depressive features

questions.explanation:
In severe premenstrual syndrome, the response rate for SSRIs is 60-90% compared to 30-40% for placebo. The e�ective medications include
both SSRIs and the SNRI Venlafaxine. The two most studied SSRIs are �uoxetine and sertraline. The most e�ective drug is Fluoxetine; it
shows response within one menstrual cycle which is too rapid to be a true antidepressant e�ect.

questions.question_text: Which of the following substance is implicated in epilepsy-related depression seen in patients treated with certain anticonvulsants?
questions.explanation:
Folate de�ciency may be a cause of depression in psychiatric patients. Patients with epilepsy have a lower folate serum level than control
subjects. The reduction in serum folate is associated with the induction of enzymes by antiepileptic drugs.

questions.question_text:
Mr. X su�ers from sweating, fatigue, heat intolerance, weight loss, weakness, �ne tremor, and tachycardia. What is the most commonly seen
psychiatric diagnosis associated with this condition?
questions.explanation: Hyperthyroidism can cause many of the same symptoms of generalized anxiety disorder and must be ruled out

questions.question_text: Which of the following can increase the likelihood of neurotoxicity when prescribed with lithium?
questions.explanation:
Lithium and haloperidol form a useful combo and is widely used. But reports of neurotoxicity suggest that if lithium is in higher end of
serum range with high dose of haloperidol use, delirium and other acute neurotoxic e�ects could emerge. (See Maudsley guidelines 2006
page 114)

questions.question_text: Dysthymia is seen in what proportion of the general population?
questions.explanation: The lifetime prevalence of dysthymia in the general population is approximately 5%. (M: F=1:2)

questions.question_text:
A 43-year-old woman works as a medical secretary. She is having signi�cant problems with personal debts and believes that with oncoming
global economic recession she will go bankrupt and may end up 'living on charity'. Which of the following cognitive distortion is she having?
questions.explanation:
In catastrophic thinking, subjects predict the worst possible catastrophic outcome from a process despite having equal or better
probabilities of other di�erent outcomes.

questions.question_text: CBT is contraindicated in
questions.explanation: In severe dementia, cognitive approaches are not useful and must be avoided if possible in those who are prone to catastrophic reactions.

questions.question_text: A child is abused by her step-father. You want to �nd out if her sibling has a similar risk. What is the best way to deal with this?

options.text: Family therapy with the abuser as well present

questions.explanation:
A single session with the child would provide a platform for exploration of risk, which would then inform whether psychotherapy is
necessary/warranted. You wouldn't set up psychotherapy straight away without knowing if it were indicated.

questions.question_text: Social phobia is most likely to be associated with which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Social phobia is characterised by severe anxiety restricted to a particular social situation, leading to avoidance that social situation. This
anxiety is not secondary to delusional or obsessive thoughts.

questions.question_text: A 77-year-old man comes to A&E with agitation and confusion. What is the most appropriate drug to prescribe?
questions.explanation:
The most likely diagnosis in this situation is Delirium. In terms of pharmacological management, oral antipsychotic medication should be
tried �rst. They are the main stay of treatment, e�ective in all types of delirium and are helpful in controlling agitation and aggressive
behaviour. Oral haloperidol is the drug of choice and has been found to be e�ective in some RCTs. The usual dose recommended for the
elderly is 0.5-1 mg BD. (Ref: Oxford Handbook of Old Age Psychiatry-pg92)

questions.question_text:
A 75-year-old man is taking Aspirin and Selegiline for his movement disorder. He is unable to work due to problems with his memory. The
correct drug of choice in his treatment is;
questions.explanation:
This man is probably su�ering from Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD). Rivastigmine has been evaluated in the symptomatic treatment of
patients with mild-to-moderate dementia associated with idiopathic Parkinson's disease. The mode of administration could be oral or a
transdermal patch. Although the evidence is preliminary, it is the best available evidence among the other options for Parkinson's related
dementia. Rivastigmine appears to improve both cognition and activities of daily living in patients with PDD, resulting in a clinically
meaningful bene�t in a large number of cases. (Ref: Emre M, Aarsland D, Albanese A et al. Rivastigmine for dementia associated with
Parkinson's disease. N Engl J Med 2004;351:2509-2518)

questions.question_text:
A 70-year-old man who was previously �t and well has reported that three months ago when he was in a supermarket, he started crying
uncontrollably for no reason. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
This person is exhibiting pseudobulbar a�ect, which is also called emotional incontinence or emotional lability. It is most commonly
observed in people with traumatic brain injury, stroke, Parkinson's disease and dementia including Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question_text:
A 65-year-old woman has a history of cognitive impairment and behavioural disturbance for more than a year. She has hypertension,
diabetes and hypercholesterolemia. MMSE score is 19/30. CT brain scan shows multiple white matter hyperintensities. The most important
initial treatment is
questions.explanation:
The diagnosis is vascular dementia. The management options are currently very limited and focus on controlling the underlying risk factors
for cerebrovascular disease. Daily aspirin may delay the course of the disease. None of the currently available drugs is licensed for vascular
dementia in the UK.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of paraphrenia in elderly above the age of 65 is
questions.explanation:
People with late paraphrenia represent approximately 10% of the elderly population of psychiatric hospitals. The reported prevalence of the
disorder among the elderly living in the community ranges from 0.1 to 4%, and its incidence has been estimated to be between 10-26 per
100 000 per year. (Almeida, O. P., Howard, R., Forstl, H., et al. (1992) Late paraphrenia: a review. International Journal of Geriatric Psychiatry,
7, 543-548.)

questions.question_text: Binge eating is seen in what proportion of patients with Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation:
Bulimic behaviour may be a result of improper brain functioning due to Alzheimer's. It is di�cult to manage, as mostly the Alzheimer's brain
is unable to process any instructions regarding the restrictions on eating and the person is unable to control binging and purging cycle. It is
seen in 10% of patients with AD.

questions.question_text: Proportion of patients with variant for of CJD that present with cerebellar ataxia is given by
questions.explanation:
The early clinical presentation of vCJD resembles kuru and consists of behavioural and psychiatric disturbances, peripheral sensory
disturbance and cerebellar ataxia. Common early psychiatric features include dysphoria, withdrawal, anxiety, insomnia, and apathy.
Neurological symptoms have preceded psychiatric symptoms in 15% of cases studied, and are present in combination with psychiatric
symptoms in 22% of cases from the onset of disease (Spencer et al., BMJ. 2002 Jun 22;324(7352):1479-82.). About 10% of vCJD cases present
with cerebellar ataxia rather than cognitive impairment, so-called ataxic vCJD.(Wadsworth et al., 2003)

questions.question_text: In old age, what percentage of patients that commit suicide have seen their GP on the same day of their suicide?
questions.explanation:
The percentage of older patients who committed suicide that visited their primary care physician- 20% on the same day as their suicide, 40-
50% within 1 week and 70% within one month.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of Alzheimer's dementia in elderly above the age of 95 is
questions.explanation:
The prevalence of dementia increases exponentially with age. About one-third of the population aged 85 and over has dementia, with
prevalence ranging from 0.4% under 60 years to 45% at 95 years and over.

questions.question_text: In patients older than 70 years of age, the rate of progression from Mild Cognitive Impairment to full-blown dementia in a year is
questions.explanation:
While the rate of progression to dementia is 1-2% for cognitively normal individuals aged 65 or older, the rates for all MCI entities are
systematically higher and most studies report rate between 10 and 15 % per annum, generally over 5 year periods.

questions.question_text:
A four-year-old boy who was born in India presents with epilepsy, severe mental retardation and behavioural problems. On examination,
you note the lack of pigment in skin and hair. The diagnosis is
questions.explanation:
Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an autosomal recessive metabolic genetic disorder. A defect in Phenylalanine Hydroxylase (PAH) or cofactor
(biopterin) with accumulation of phenylalanine. Symptoms absent neonatally, a later development of seizures (25% generalized). Clinical
features include fair skin, blue eyes, blond hair, and recurrent rashes. Untreated infants have an unusual mouse-like body odour.
Microcephaly is seen in 50% of cases. Without treatment mild to profound mental retardation, language delay, destructiveness, self-injury,
hyperactivity could result. A low-phenylalanine diet must be usually continued throughout the childhood.

questions.question_text:
A 7-year-old boy has a moderate degree of learning disability. He is socially disinhibited and excessively friendly. These are behavioural
phenotypes of which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
Williams syndrome- is characterised by hypercalcemia (50% of cases) with supra valvular aortic stenosis and unusual facies. It is a rare
condition. The majority of these subjects have a mild to moderate degree of mental retardation. Clinical features include short stature,
growth retardation, unusual facial features including broad forehead, el�n-like facies, hoarse voice, premature wrinkling and sagging of the
skin, renal and cardiovascular abnormalities (supra valvular aortic stenosis); thyroid abnormalities; hypercalcemia. Behavioural phenotypes
include: Anxiety, hypersensitivity or outgoing, sociable, disinhibited, excessive friendliness.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of schizophrenia in the learning disabled population is
questions.explanation:
Psychotic disorders, particularly schizophrenia, appear to be more common in those who also have a learning disability. The rate is raised
threefold over the general population. Most studies report a prevalence of 3 to 3.5 percent for schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Deletion of a segment of chromosome 15q or the segment being solely derived from maternal chromosome leads to
questions.explanation:
The genomic imprinting syndromes of Angelman and Prader-Willi can be inherited in two di�erent ways. The most common mechanism is a
complete deletion of the segment (no gene copies left). The second mechanism is called uniparental disomy where the segments do not go
missing, but instead, are derived solely from one parent. In the latter case, maternal inheritance of the segment (maternal UPD) leads to
Prader-Willi while paternal UPD leads to Angelman's.

questions.question_text: The highest incidence of intellectual disabilities is seen in
questions.explanation:
The prevalence of intellectual disabilities at any one time is estimated to range from 1 percent to 3 percent of the population. The incidence
of intellectual disabilities is di�cult to calculate because mild intellectual disability sometimes goes unrecognised until middle childhood. The
highest incidence is in school-age children, with the peak at ages 10 to 14 years. Intellectual disabilities are about 1.5 times more common
among men than among women. Those with severe or profound disabilities have high mortality rates because of the complications of
associated physical disorders.

questions.question_text: Lyonisation is a feature associated with which of the following disorders?
questions.explanation:
Whenever there are more than 1 (haploid) set of X-linked genes in a cell, all but one of the genes are inactivated at random and have no
phenotypic expression. This process, called Lyonization, is inherently random explaining the more variability in the expression of certain X-
linked disorders in women. In individuals with the Klinefelter (XXY) karyotype who are phenotypically male, Lyonization silences the extra set
of X genes.

questions.question_text: All the following disorders have been found to be signi�cantly comorbid with pathological gambling except
questions.explanation:
Impulse control underlies the mechanism of pathological gambling. Hence, high degree of comorbid ADHD, substance use and other
impulse control disorders are found. Depression is also highly correlated.

questions.question_text:
A 24 years old male has repeated emotional outbursts and is impulsive. He has been arrested on numerous occasions for assaulting his
partner. Most likely diagnosis is
questions.explanation: This patient is exhibiting antisocial traits.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of psychosis in prison population is
questions.explanation:
The weighted prevalence of probable functional psychosis in the past year was 4.5 per thousand (95% CI=3.1 to 5.8) in the household survey.
In the prison survey, the weighted prevalence was over ten times greater: 52 per thousand (95% CI=45 to 60). Apart from a minority of
